bounded-context.name: Billing
bounded-context.purpose: Invoicing, payment capture, refunds. Consumes , opens an invoice, drives the out-of-process payment gateway, records the resulting . No business logic about *what* to charge — only *how* to collect.

term.name: `Invoice`
term.definition: A demand for payment, scoped to one Order. Carries the line items as captured at order-placed time, plus tax computed from the overlay. Immutable once issued; amendments produce a new Invoice + credit note pair.
term.identity-rule: Stable by `invoiceId`. Invoices have a human-readable serial (`INV-2026-000042`) that is *not* the identity — serials may be renumbered for legal reasons; the invoiceId never changes.

term.name: `Payment`
term.definition: The capture record returned by the payment gateway: amount, currency, gateway transaction id, settled-at timestamp. Refunds are negative-amount Payments against the same Invoice.
term.identity-rule: Stable by `paymentId`. The gateway transaction id is a *correlation* key, not identity — gateway-side renumbering would not change our paymentId.

term.name: `settlePayment`
term.definition: Drives the payment gateway to capture funds for an Invoice. On success, persists a Payment and emits . On hard failure, marks the Invoice `payment-failed` and emits a separate (unmodeled here) failure event.

term.name: `PaymentSettled`
term.definition: Emitted when a Payment lands successfully. The signal Shipping waits on before releasing the order to fulfillment.
term.emitted-when: The gateway returns a settled status for a Payment and the row is persisted.

invariant.name: Refunds cannot exceed captured amount
invariant.statement: For any Invoice, `Σ refundedMinor ≤ Σ capturedMinor`. A refund attempt that would breach the inequality is rejected before hitting the gateway.
invariant.rationale: Refunding more than was captured is the kind of mistake that makes for a fraud alert and an awkward customer-support escalation. The gateway will *also* reject most of these, but catching them at our edge keeps the audit log clean and gives the operator a clear error message.

seam.name: Billing ↔ External payment gateway
seam.description: Billing accepts the payment gateway's data shapes (PCI-compliant payment-method tokens, ISO-4217 currency codes, settlement status enums) directly. No translation layer. Our `Payment` entity is mostly a renamed projection of the gateway's `Transaction` record.
seam.rationale: Writing an ACL here would mean re-inventing PCI-DSS field names to suit Shopwell's house style — pure cost, no benefit. The gateway's model is well-documented, stable across years, and shared with every PSP integration our payments team has touched. Conforming is the honest move.
